Summary of the Solving Trajectory - Objective: Retrieve authoritative EC (EINECS/REACH) numbers for two chemicals explicitly used in the virus testing methods of Adikini et al. (2016): (1) p‑nitrophenyl phosphate substrate used in DAS/TAS ELISA (commonly disodium salt; Sigma pNPP substrate), and (2) nitrocellulose (cellulose nitrate) used as the membrane in NCM‑ELISA. For each: provide EC number, CAS number, names/synonyms, and reliable source links (ECHA pages and/or official SDS), and explain variants and cases where EC numbers do not exist (polymer list numbers). Step-by-step actions and tool results: 1. Searched ECHA for p‑nitrophenyl phosphate disodium entries and found an ECHA page listing “sodium bis(4‑nitrophenyl) phosphate” (a diester) with EC 223‑739‑2 and CAS 4043‑96‑3. This helped distinguish diester vs monoester. - Result: Pre-registered substances page snippet showing “sodium bis(4-nitrophenyl) phosphate. 223-739-2. 4043-96-3.” 2. Searched for CAS 4043‑96‑3 and confirmed it corresponds to “Bis(p‑nitrophenyl) phosphate sodium salt,” not the ELISA substrate. - Result: Sigma page listing “Bis(p‑nitrophenyl) phosphate sodium salt,” CAS 4043-96-3. 3. Searched ECHA for “4‑nitrophenyl phosphate disodium”; found ECHA CHEM identity and pre-registered pages indicating “Disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate” with EC 224‑246‑5 and CAS 4264‑83‑9. - Result: ECHA CHEM links (identity and dossier), plus pre-registered page showing “disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate. 224‑246‑5. 4264‑83‑9.” 4. Searched ECHA for nitrocellulose (cellulose nitrate); found ECHA Substance Information infocard for “nitrocellulose.” - Result: ECHA substance page showing “EC / List no.: 936-908-7” and CAS not displayed. 5. Attempted to scrape ECHA CHEM identity page for disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate; the page did not render content via scraping (dynamic), but the identity and dossier URLs were confirmed via search results. 6. Scraped ECHA pre-registered substances page; captured the table row explicitly showing “disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate | 224‑246‑5 | 4264‑83‑9.” 7. Scraped nitrocellulose ECHA substance page; captured infocard content including “EC / List no.: 936‑908‑7.” 8. Searched Sigma/Merck for pNPP SDS/product pages confirming hydrate naming and CAS 4264‑83‑9. - Result: Multiple Sigma product pages confirm “p‑Nitrophenyl phosphate, disodium salt, hexahydrate,” CAS 4264‑83‑9, used as ELISA substrate. 9. Searched for nitrocellulose membrane SDS from reputable vendors; found: - Merck/Sigma SDS pages for nitrocellulose membrane filters. - Sartorius CN membrane product page listing CAS 9004‑70‑0. - Cytiva/GE Life Sciences SDS PDF for nitrocellulose membrane filters. - Thermo product page noting flammability. Key findings: - Disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate (monoester pNPP) has EC 224‑246‑5 and CAS 4264‑83‑9 on ECHA. - Bis(p‑nitrophenyl) phosphate sodium salt (diester) is a different substance with EC 223‑739‑2 and CAS 4043‑96‑3; not the ELISA substrate used. - Nitrocellulose is a polymer; ECHA assigns an ECHA List number (936‑908‑7), not an EC number. Vendors’ SDS for nitrocellulose membranes consistently use CAS 9004‑70‑0. FINAL ANSWER Chemicals and identifiers relevant to Adikini et al. (2016) virus testing methods: 1) p‑Nitrophenyl phosphate substrate used in DAS/TAS ELISA (commonly supplied as disodium salt; Sigma pNPP substrate) - EC (EINECS/REACH): 224‑246‑5 - CAS: 4264‑83‑9 - IUPAC name: Disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate - Trivial names/synonyms: - p‑Nitrophenyl phosphate disodium salt (pNPP) - 4‑Nitrophenyl phosphate disodium salt - p‑Nitrophenyl phosphate disodium salt hexahydrate (common commercial hydrate form) - PNPP - Most appropriate variant and explanation: - The ELISA substrate for alkaline phosphatase is the monoester disodium salt (EC 224‑246‑5; CAS 4264‑83‑9). A different substance, the diester “bis(p‑nitrophenyl) phosphate sodium salt,” has EC 223‑739‑2 and CAS 4043‑96‑3 and is not the ELISA substrate. - Commercial pNPP is often sold as the disodium hexahydrate. Hydrates do not receive separate EC numbers; vendors commonly associate the same CAS 4264‑83‑9 with the hydrate form. - Authoritative sources and citations: - ECHA pre-registered substances (explicit row): - Quote: “disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate | 224‑246‑5 | 4264‑83‑9” - URL: https://echa.europa.eu/de/information-on-chemicals/pre-registered-substances?p_p_id=disslists_WAR_disslistsportlet&p_p_lifecycle=0&p_p_state=normal&p_p_mode=view&_disslists_WAR_disslistsportlet_cur=286&_disslists_WAR_disslistsportlet_delta=100&_disslists_WAR_disslistsportlet_orderByCol=diss_registration_date&_disslists_WAR_disslistsportlet_orderByType=asc - ECHA CHEM identity/dossier: - Identity (Disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate; EC 224‑246‑5; CAS 4264‑83‑9): https://chem.echa.europa.eu/100.022.042/identity - Dossier list: https://chem.echa.europa.eu/100.022.042/dossier-list - Vendor SDS/product pages: - Merck/Sigma p‑Nitrophenyl Phosphate, Disodium Salt, Hexahydrate (ELISA substrate): https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/ES/en/product/mm/4876 - Sigma CAS search page listing pNPP disodium salt forms including hexahydrate under CAS 4264‑83‑9: https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/VI/en/search/4264-83-9?focus=products&type=cas_number Note on a different variant (not appropriate for ELISA substrate): - Bis(p‑nitrophenyl) phosphate sodium salt (diester) - EC: 223‑739‑2 - CAS: 4043‑96‑3 - ECHA listing (pre-registered substances): - Quote: “sodium bis(4‑nitrophenyl) phosphate. 223‑739‑2. 4043‑96‑3.” - URL: https://echa.europa.eu/da/information-on-chemicals/pre-registered-substances?p_p_id=disslists_WAR_disslistsportlet&_disslists_WAR_disslistsportlet_cur=238 2) Nitrocellulose (cellulose nitrate) used as the membrane in NCM‑ELISA - EC number: None (polymers are generally not in the EC Inventory) - ECHA List number: 936‑908‑7 - CAS: 9004‑70‑0 (polymer CAS used in SDS and membrane products) - Trivial names/synonyms: - Nitrocellulose - Cellulose nitrate - Collodion (solutions or films of nitrocellulose) - Nitrocellulose membrane; cellulose nitrate (CN) membrane filter - Most appropriate identifier and explanation: - Nitrocellulose is a polymer; ECHA does not assign an EC number. An “ECHA List number” is used instead. The ECHA substance page for nitrocellulose shows List number 936‑908‑7 and does not display a CAS on the infocard. - For product identification in laboratory use (ELISA membranes), reputable vendors’ SDS and product pages consistently use CAS 9004‑70‑0 for nitrocellulose/cellulose nitrate membranes. - Authoritative sources and citations: - ECHA Substance Information page (Infocard): - Quote: “EC / List no.: 936‑908‑7” (CAS not displayed) - URL: https://echa.europa.eu/substance-information/-/substanceinfo/100.219.022 - Vendor SDS and product documentation: - Merck/Sigma SDS for Nitrocellulose membrane filters: - HAWP04700 SDS: https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/sds/mm/hawp04700 - GSWP04700 SDS: https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/sds/mm/gswp04700 - DAWP04700 SDS: https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/sds/mm/dawp04700 - Sartorius CN membrane filter product page explicitly listing CAS 9004‑70‑0: - Quote: “CAS. 9004‑70‑0” - URL: https://shop.sartorius.com/us/p/cellulose-nitrate-cn-membrane-filter/13004--80----ALN - Cytiva/GE SDS for nitrocellulose membrane filters (PDF): - URL: https://d3.cytivalifesciences.com/prod/SDS/28420741%20AU%20EN.pdf - Additional vendor reference (collodion/nitrocellulose CAS 9004‑70‑0): https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/US/en/product/sigma/09817 Detailed Supporting Information and Relevant Quotes - ECHA pre-registered substances page (Disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate): - “disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate | 224‑246‑5 | 4264‑83‑9” - Page context confirms EC and CAS identifiers for the monoester disodium salt. - ECHA CHEM identity/dossier pages (Disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate): - Identity page title/snippet indicates “Disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate; EC number 224‑246‑5; CAS number 4264‑83‑9.” - ECHA pre-registered substances page (diester variant): - “sodium bis(4‑nitrophenyl) phosphate. 223‑739‑2. 4043‑96‑3.” - Distinct from the ELISA substrate; included to document variant and avoid misassignment. - ECHA Substance Information page (Nitrocellulose): - Infocard explicitly shows: “EC / List no.: 936‑908‑7” and “CAS no.: –” (not displayed), consistent with polymer treatment. - Vendor documentation (nitrocellulose CAS): - Sartorius CN membrane page: “CAS. 9004‑70‑0” - Merck/Sigma nitrocellulose membrane filter SDS pages identify the product class and transport hazard, consistent with nitrocellulose/cellulose nitrate composition. - Vendor documentation (pNPP ELISA substrate): - Merck/Sigma p‑Nitrophenyl Phosphate, Disodium Salt, Hexahydrate product page indicates ELISA substrate use and associates CAS 4264‑83‑9 with hexahydrate form; typical synonyms include “4‑Nitrophenyl phosphate disodium salt hexahydrate; p‑Nitrophenyl phosphate disodium hexahydrate.” Notes on Variants and Appropriateness - pNPP: - Monoester disodium salt is the ELISA substrate (EC 224‑246‑5; CAS 4264‑83‑9). Commercial hydrate (hexahydrate) is common; hydrates do not have separate EC numbers. The diester “bis(p‑nitrophenyl) phosphate” has different identifiers (EC 223‑739‑2; CAS 4043‑96‑3) and is not appropriate for ELISA. - Nitrocellulose: - As a polymer, nitrocellulose does not have an EC (EINECS) number. ECHA assigns an ECHA List number (936‑908‑7). CAS 9004‑70‑0 is widely used by manufacturers and SDS for nitrocellulose membranes and is appropriate for product identification in NCM‑ELISA. Reliability and Cross-checks - ECHA pages are authoritative for EC/List numbers. The pre-registered substances page provides explicit EC and CAS for Disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate. The nitrocellulose infocard shows the List number format and lack of CAS display, consistent with polymer treatment. - Multiple reputable vendor SDS/product pages corroborate nitrocellulose CAS 9004‑70‑0 and pNPP ELISA substrate naming and usage, including hydrate forms. Conclusion - p‑Nitrophenyl phosphate disodium (ELISA substrate): EC 224‑246‑5; CAS 4264‑83‑9; names include p‑Nitrophenyl phosphate disodium salt (monoester), with common hexahydrate form; ECHA pages and Sigma/Merck documentation confirm identifiers and ELISA usage. - Nitrocellulose (cellulose nitrate) membrane: No EC number; ECHA List number 936‑908‑7; CAS 9004‑70‑0 used by SDS and manufacturers for membrane products; ECHA substance page confirms list number assignment for the polymer. Links (for direct reference) - Disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate (ECHA CHEM identity): https://chem.echa.europa.eu/100.022.042/identity - Disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate (ECHA CHEM dossier list): https://chem.echa.europa.eu/100.022.042/dossier-list - Disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate entry (ECHA pre-registered substances): https://echa.europa.eu/de/information-on-chemicals/pre-registered-substances?p_p_id=disslists_WAR_disslistsportlet&_disslists_WAR_disslistsportlet_cur=286 - Nitrocellulose (ECHA substance information infocard): https://echa.europa.eu/substance-information/-/substanceinfo/100.219.022 - Sigma pNPP product page (ELISA substrate, hexahydrate): https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/ES/en/product/mm/4876 - Sigma CAS listing page for 4264‑83‑9: https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/VI/en/search/4264-83-9?focus=products&type=cas_number - Sigma/Merck nitrocellulose membrane SDS pages: https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/sds/mm/hawp04700, https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/sds/mm/gswp04700, https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/sds/mm/dawp04700 - Sartorius CN membrane product page (CAS 9004‑70‑0): https://shop.sartorius.com/us/p/cellulose-nitrate-cn-membrane-filter/13004--80----ALN - Cytiva/GE nitrocellulose membrane SDS (PDF): https://d3.cytivalifesciences.com/prod/SDS/28420741%20AU%20EN.pdf This report contains all gathered information and the final authoritative identifiers required for the subtask.

Comprehensive Summary and Final Report Objective - Identify the 2016 Uganda-based paper explicitly involving Sweet potato feathery mottle virus (SPFMV) and Sweet potato chlorotic stunt virus (SPCSV) (“Pearl of Africa”), confirm its virus testing method(s), and determine the EC (EINECS/REACH) numbers of the two most commonly used chemicals for that method. - Provide a transparent, complete report of all findings, reasoning, alternatives, and uncertainties. - Output the final answer as the two EC numbers, semicolon-separated, ordered by the alphabetized chemical names. Solving Trajectory and Tool Use - Step 1: Locate the paper and extract diagnostic methods and reagents. - Tool used: Web agent to search and retrieve full text and metadata. - Results: - Paper identified: Adikini et al. (2016), Journal of Phytopathology. - Title: Effects of Sweet Potato Feathery Mottle Virus and Sweet Potato Chlorotic Stunt Virus on the Yield of SweetPotato in Uganda. - Authors: Scovia Adikini; Settumba B. Mukasa; Robert O. M. Mwanga; Richard W. Gibson. - Journal details: Journal of Phytopathology, 2016, Volume 164, Issue 4, Pages 242–254. - DOI: 10.1111/jph.12451. - Full text links: - Open-access PDF: https://cgspace.cgiar.org/bitstreams/26326f58-2d19-484f-a92e-ff4b612476a6/download - Repository item: https://cgspace.cgiar.org/items/02591cd5-70f7-4c28-8880-48f8cc319f21 - DOI page: https://doi.org/10.1111/jph.12451 - Country context: Uganda (the “Pearl of Africa”), with field sites at MUARIK and NaSARRI. - Virus testing methods used: - NCM-ELISA (Nitrocellulose Membrane ELISA) for broad screening across ten sweetpotato viruses. - DAS-ELISA specifically for SPFMV detection and titre estimation. - TAS-ELISA specifically for SPCSV detection and titre estimation. - Graft indexing onto Ipomoea setosa for infection verification. - Key diagnostic reagents/materials in the paper: - “appropriate ELISA extraction buffer” (composition not specified). - NCM-ELISA protocol and positive controls (CIP Lima, Peru). - DAS-ELISA kit for SPFMV with IgG and IgG–AP (DSMZ). - TAS-ELISA kit for SPCSV with rabbit IgG, mouse MAb, and rabbit anti-mouse IgG–AP (DSMZ). - Substrate: p-nitrophenyl phosphate (pNPP), from Sigma Chemical Co. - Microplates: Sigma Chemical Co. - Reader: Bio-Rad model 680; absorbance 405 nm after 1.5 hours. - Relevant quotes: - Sampling and extraction: “ground in a polyvinyl bag using appropriate enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) extraction buffer.” - NCM-ELISA: “Nitrocellulose membrane ELISA was carried out following the protocol obtained from CIP Lima, Peru…” - DAS/TAS ELISA: “using protocol by Clark and Adams (1977).” - Substrate: “The p-nitrophenyl phosphate substrate and microplates used were from Sigma Chemical Co.” - Step 2: Retrieve EC/EINECS or ECHA List numbers for the two selected chemicals used in the virus testing methods. - Tool used: Web agent to query ECHA and vendor SDS/product documentation. - Results: - p-Nitrophenyl phosphate disodium salt (monoester): - ECHA confirms EC 224-246-5 and CAS 4264-83-9 for Disodium 4-nitrophenyl phosphate. - Common ELISA substrate form is disodium salt, frequently sold as hexahydrate; hydrates do not have separate EC numbers. - Sources: - ECHA (pre-registered substances): “disodium 4‑nitrophenyl phosphate | 224‑246‑5 | 4264‑83‑9” - ECHA CHEM identity/dossier pages: https://chem.echa.europa.eu/100.022.042/identity; https://chem.echa.europa.eu/100.022.042/dossier-list - Sigma/Merck product page (ELISA substrate, hexahydrate): https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/ES/en/product/mm/4876 - Sigma CAS search for 4264-83-9: https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/VI/en/search/4264-83-9?focus=products&type=cas_number - Important distinction: The diester variant “sodium bis(4-nitrophenyl) phosphate” has EC 223-739-2 and CAS 4043-96-3, but it is not the ELISA substrate used by the paper. - Nitrocellulose (cellulose nitrate) membrane: - Nitrocellulose is a polymer; polymers generally have no EINECS EC number. ECHA provides an “EC/List number” instead. - ECHA infocard shows List no. 936-908-7 for nitrocellulose. - Vendors’ SDS and product pages commonly use CAS 9004-70-0 for nitrocellulose membrane filters. - Sources: - ECHA substance infocard: https://echa.europa.eu/substance-information/-/substanceinfo/100.219.022 (shows EC/List no.: 936-908-7). - Sartorius CN membrane product page (CAS 9004-70-0): https://shop.sartorius.com/us/p/cellulose-nitrate-cn-membrane-filter/13004--80----ALN - Sigma/Merck nitrocellulose membrane SDS examples: https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/sds/mm/hawp04700; https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/sds/mm/gswp04700; https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/sds/mm/dawp04700 - Cytiva/GE nitrocellulose membrane SDS (PDF): https://d3.cytivalifesciences.com/prod/SDS/28420741%20AU%20EN.pdf Interpretation of “Two Most Commonly Used Chemicals” - Within the virus testing methods detailed (NCM-ELISA; DAS-ELISA; TAS-ELISA): - Nitrocellulose membrane is fundamental to NCM-ELISA, used for broad screening across multiple viruses. It is a standard, widely used material in serological membrane ELISA workflows. - p-Nitrophenyl phosphate (pNPP) is the standard alkaline phosphatase (AP) ELISA substrate used in microplate ELISAs (DAS/TAS) to produce a colorimetric signal measured at 405 nm. It is the primary “chemical” reagent explicitly named for detection across ELISA procedures. - Other materials mentioned include ELISA extraction buffer (unspecified composition), antibodies and AP conjugates (proteins/enzymes, not assigned EINECS chemical EC numbers), microplates (likely polystyrene; polymer chemicals but not explicitly identified in the paper). - Based on explicit mentions and common ELISA practice, the two chemicals most central and widely used across the stated virus testing method are nitrocellulose (for NCM-ELISA) and p-nitrophenyl phosphate (for DAS/TAS ELISA). Alternative or Conflicting Candidates and Resolution - ELISA extraction buffer: Composition not specified; without explicit chemical identity, EC numbers cannot be assigned. - Antibody conjugates (IgG-AP): These are biomolecules and do not have EINECS EC numbers; alkaline phosphatase has enzyme commission (EC) 3.1.3.1, but this is a different numbering system unrelated to the requested “chemicals” context. - Microplates: Identified only by supplier; material (e.g., polystyrene) not specified in the paper; even if polymer EC/List numbers exist, they were not explicitly stated or necessary to the chemical reagent use in detection. Chemical Identity Verification and Numbers - p-Nitrophenyl phosphate (disodium salt; ELISA substrate): - EC (EINECS/REACH): 224-246-5. - CAS: 4264-83-9. - Names/synonyms: Disodium 4-nitrophenyl phosphate; p-Nitrophenyl phosphate disodium salt; p-Nitrophenyl phosphate disodium salt hexahydrate (commercial); PNPP. - Nitrocellulose (cellulose nitrate) membrane: - EC number: Not applicable (polymer). - ECHA List number: 936-908-7. - CAS: 9004-70-0 (commonly used in SDS and membrane products). - Names/synonyms: Nitrocellulose; Cellulose nitrate; Collodion; Nitrocellulose membrane; CN membrane. Alphabetization and Output Formatting - Chemical names alphabetized: nitrocellulose; p-nitrophenyl phosphate. - Order of EC numbers accordingly: List number for nitrocellulose first (936-908-7), then EC number for p-nitrophenyl phosphate (224-246-5). - Output format: strictly two numbers, semicolon-separated, no spaces or extra characters. Final Answer 936-908-7;224-246-5 Direct Quotes and Supporting Evidence from the Paper (Adikini et al., 2016) - “Nitrocellulose membrane ELISA was carried out following the protocol obtained from CIP Lima, Peru…” - “Additional tests using DAS and TAS ELISA were specifically carried out to detect and estimate the virus titre for SPFMV or SPCSV, respectively, using protocol by Clark and Adams (1977).” - “The DAS-ELISA kit (containing coating antibody immunoglobulin G (IgG) and detecting antibody IgG-AP)… and TAS ELISA kit… were from DSMZ…” - “The p-nitrophenyl phosphate substrate and microplates used were from Sigma Chemical Co. The absorbance was measured at 405 nm after one and half hours using a Bio-Rad microplate reader (model 680).” References and Links - Paper: https://doi.org/10.1111/jph.12451; Open-access PDF: https://cgspace.cgiar.org/bitstreams/26326f58-2d19-484f-a92e-ff4b612476a6/download - ECHA (Disodium 4-nitrophenyl phosphate): - Identity: https://chem.echa.europa.eu/100.022.042/identity - Dossier list: https://chem.echa.europa.eu/100.022.042/dossier-list - Pre-registered substances (explicit EC and CAS): https://echa.europa.eu/de/information-on-chemicals/pre-registered-substances?p_p_id=disslists_WAR_disslistsportlet&_disslists_WAR_disslistsportlet_cur=286 - Vendors (pNPP ELISA substrate): https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/ES/en/product/mm/4876; https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/VI/en/search/4264-83-9?focus=products&type=cas_number - ECHA (Nitrocellulose): https://echa.europa.eu/substance-information/-/substanceinfo/100.219.022 - Vendors (Nitrocellulose membranes and SDS): - Sigma/Merck SDS: https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/sds/mm/hawp04700; https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/sds/mm/gswp04700; https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/sds/mm/dawp04700 - Sartorius: https://shop.sartorius.com/us/p/cellulose-nitrate-cn-membrane-filter/13004--80----ALN - Cytiva/GE SDS: https://d3.cytivalifesciences.com/prod/SDS/28420741%20AU%20EN.pdf Conclusion - The identified 2016 Uganda paper (Adikini et al.) used NCM-ELISA and DAS/TAS ELISA as the virus testing methods for SPFMV and SPCSV. The two most central and extensively used chemicals in these methods, as explicitly referenced, are nitrocellulose (membrane for NCM-ELISA) and p-nitrophenyl phosphate (ELISA substrate for AP detection). - Verified identifiers: Nitrocellulose has ECHA List no. 936-908-7 (polymer; no EINECS EC number), and p-NPP disodium has EC 224-246-5. Alphabetized chemical names yield the final ordered numbers. FINAL ANSWER 936-908-7;224-246-5

LLM extracted final answer: **Step-by-step Analysis:** 1. The 2016 Ugandan study (Adikini et al., 2016) used NCM-ELISA plus DAS/TAS-ELISA to test for SPFMV and SPCSV. 2. The two reagents explicitly stated and central to these methods are: • Nitrocellulose (membrane for NCM-ELISA) • p-Nitrophenyl phosphate (substrate for alkaline-phosphatase ELISA detection) 3. Their identifiers: • Nitrocellulose – ECHA List/EC number 936-908-7 • p-Nitrophenyl phosphate, disodium salt – EC number 224-246-5 4. Alphabetizing the chemical names gives the order: nitrocellulose, p-nitrophenyl phosphate. 5. Output must be the two numbers, semicolon-separated, no spaces. **Final Answer:** \boxed{936-908-7;224-246-5} **Confidence:** 80 **Supporting Evidence:** Paper cites nitrocellulose membrane ELISA and p-nitrophenyl phosphate substrate; ECHA pages list the stated EC/List numbers (936-908-7 for nitrocellulose; 224-246-5 for disodium 4-nitrophenyl phosphate). **Potential Weaknesses:** Nitrocellulose, as a polymer, technically has a “List number” rather than a classic EINECS EC number; if the question strictly requires only classic EC numbers, an alternative reagent might be expected.
